findings.title: Content-Security-Policy
findings.reason: script-src allows 'unsafe-inline' without a nonce or hash, so injected inline scripts can run
findings.fix_hint: enforce a CSP whose script-src allows no inline or wildcard scripts

platform_fixes.how: middleware (proxy): create a nonce per request, set the CSP header and read it with headers() in the layout
Rules > Transform Rules > Modify Response Header > Set static: Content-Security-Policy
platform_fixes.note: A static Transform Rule cannot add a per-request nonce; set the CSP in the app, use hashes, or a Worker

findings.remediation: CSP limits which scripts can run, which reduces what injected code (XSS) can do. Generate a new random nonce per response and put it on every <script>, or use hashes for fixed inline scripts. With nonces, also set base-uri 'self' so an injected <base> tag cannot send the page's own scripts to another site. The example is a starting point, not a drop-in policy: review the whole existing CSP, check third-party scripts and framework hydration, roll out with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, fix what it reports, then enforce.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy missing
findings.fix_hint: send a Permissions-Policy that turns off features the site does not use

platform_fixes.how: Rules > Transform Rules > Modify Response Header > Set static: Permissions-Policy
next.config.js headers(): { key: "Permissions-Policy", value: "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()" }

findings.remediation: Permissions-Policy turns off browser features (camera, microphone, location, payment) the site does not use, so injected or embedded code cannot use them. List only features the site needs with (self).

findings.title: Technology disclosure
findings.reason: x-powered-by tells attackers which software runs here
findings.fix_hint: remove X-Powered-By, version numbers and internal host names from headers and meta generator

platform_fixes.how: Rules > Transform Rules > Modify Response Header > Remove: X-Powered-By

findings.remediation: Version headers let attackers look up known vulnerabilities for your exact software without probing. Removing them is not a fix for outdated software, but it stops free reconnaissance. Keep the software updated as well. The same applies to a <meta name="generator"> tag with a version, and to internal server names in X-Backend-Server or Server-Timing.

findings.title: Strict-Transport-Security
findings.advice: add includeSubDomains once every subdomain serves HTTPS, so subdomains are protected too
